subject: TTFT / streaming SLOs — post-call recap & next steps
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
To: Chris Taylor <chris.taylor@starkretail.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 01 Jul 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: TTFT / streaming SLOs — post-call recap & next steps

Hi Chris — great to meet after the demo earlier. Quick recap from our side and suggested next steps so we can scope a short POC against your performance targets.

Recap of stated goals (please correct if I’ve misheard):
- TTFT target: 200ms median for primary web clients (mobile goal: 300ms median)
- Streaming responses required (user-visible token streaming for progressive UI) via SSE or WebSocket — you prefer WebSocket but SSE acceptable as fallback
- Chunk cadence: ~150–250ms between chunks for a good UX (small token batches, avoid large pauses)
- Throughput / concurrency: expected steady-state 150–200 RPS with bursts to 400 RPS; concurrency per model: ~50 active streams
- Availability: will need predictable latency at 95th percentile; interested in SLA options for Dedicated capacity

Immediate asks / next steps:
1) Can you share representative sample payloads and typical prompt lengths (we requested these on the call) — we included an example file attached (stark-latency-sample-payloads.json).
2) We’ll run a quick latency / streaming cadence run against our hosted profiles and share results by EOD Friday.
3) Dev (cc’d) to validate WebSocket streaming behavior and confirm if there are any SDK/connection caveats for your client stack.
4) Let’s schedule a 30-minute POC sync next week to review results and discuss Dedicated sizing. Available slots: Tue/Wed 10–12 PT.

Notes on what we’ll measure in the POC:
- TTFT (time from API request to first token) median/95/99
- Chunk cadence distribution (inter-chunk gaps) and average chunk size
- End-to-end latency under concurrency (50/100/200 streams) and under burst traffic
- Failure/fallback behavior for WebSocket vs SSE

Attaching our short brief on streaming options for reference (redwood-sse-websocket-options.pdf).

If that all looks right I’ll kick off the baseline runs and we’ll loop back with numbers and a link to a shared dashboard.

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Thanks Aditya — that summary is spot on. A few clarifications from our side:
- We validated internally that 200ms median TTFT is the right bar for desktop web. Mobile relaxed target (300ms) is fine.
- We strongly prefer WebSocket for streaming (mobile SDKs already use WS-based channels), but want a documented fallback to SSE for edge cases (corporate proxies).
- Chunk cadence: aiming for ~200ms average gaps, but willing to tolerate a small number of 400–500ms gaps during long generation tokens. UX team will test with your sample cadence results.
- Throughput: our initial horizon is 150 RPS average with 300 RPS burst capacity; concurrency of 50 active streaming sessions is accurate.

We attached a short dump of sample prompts (same file you included) and a short internal doc on how we surface streaming chunks in the UI. Our engineering manager (cc’d) will join the POC sync.

Can you confirm whether your hosted profiles support prioritized requests (we have mixed critical/low priority queues) and whether batching will affect TTFT for these streams?

Happy to meet Tue 10:30 PT.

Best,
Chris Taylor
Sr. Manager, AI Products — Stark Retail
chris.taylor@starkretail.com

Subject: Re: TTFT / streaming SLOs — post-call recap & next steps

Thanks Chris — great context. Quick answers while we prep the POC runs:
- Prioritization: yes — our routing layer supports request priority tags and soft-priority queues. For strict TTFT SLOs we recommend a high-priority lane (reservation or Dedicated capacity) so batching and background optimizations don’t increase first-token latency.
- Batching: continuous batching improves throughput but can add variable latency if requests wait to be batched. For streaming TTFT-sensitive calls we typically tune batching thresholds/timeouts aggressively (very small batch windows) or use dedicated capacity to avoid batching-induced queuing.
- WebSocket vs SSE: WebSocket is preferred for your case. Dev will validate SDK behavior and confirm any keep-alive/idle settings we recommend.

Planned next steps from Redwood:
1) Dev will run two baseline tests today against our hosted-low-latency profile: (a) 1:1 no-batching streams to measure TTFT, (b) small-batch mode to show batching impact on TTFT and chunk cadence.
2) We’ll share a dashboard link + CSV with median/95/99 TTFT and chunk-time percentiles by EOD.
3) Confirm POC sync Tue 10:30 PT and we’ll invite infra/engineering for the deep-dive.

@Dev — can you run the following today:
- 1k requests single-threaded to measure cold vs warm KV-cache TTFT
- 10k requests across concurrent streams at concurrency levels 10/50/100 to gather percentile curves
- capture inter-chunk timing histogram and attach the CSV

Thanks — I’ll put a calendar invite for Tue 10:30 PT once we have the baseline numbers.

-Aditya

Looping in quick update from the ops run:
- Completed runs: cold vs warm KV-cache, concurrency sweeps at 10/50/100. Attached CSVs and the small dashboard link (I’ll drop into the shared collection).
- Early findings: hosted-low-latency profile hits median TTFT ~180ms warm and ~240ms cold for 1:1 streams; 95th climbs to ~420ms at concurrency 100 under burst.
- Chunk cadence: median inter-chunk gap ~210ms; 90th ~380ms. Small-batch mode increased median TTFT by ~35ms on average.

Notes / recommendations:
- For guaranteed 200ms median at your expected concurrency, recommend Dedicated capacity with high-priority reservation.
- WebSocket is confirmed as the recommended streaming transport for lower client-side overhead; we’ll provide sample keep-alive settings and a JS + native mobile snippet.
- If you must use hosted shared profiles, we can add a soft-priority tag and set a low batch window, but TTFT will be less consistent under burst.

Attaching files: latency-results-stark.csv, chunk-cadence-histogram.csv. I’ll add the dashboard link to the HubSpot deal.

I’ll join Tue’s sync and be prepared to walk the percentile graphs.

- Dev
